title: Dobrzy czy dobre?
title_en: Plural adjectives for a group with a man in it
note:
C1 Block 2, unit 5 (C1-SPINE O2) - the VIRILE plural adjective, the men-group form, and the last teaching unit of the block.

FOUR NEW FORMS, one idea: nowi, mlodzi, zmeczeni (the virile Nominative plural) and zmeczone (the non-virile plural of the same adjective, needed so the split has both sides on one word). dobrzy is RECYCLED, not taught - b1_virile_reco [109] handed it over as a whole ready-made form with no rule at all, and b1_virile_nom [110] re-used it as a predicate recall item on the same footing. So the unit's shape is the b2_verbal_nouns / b2_participle_pass anchor shape: a form the learner has read since B1 turns out to be built by a pattern, and three more adjectives get theirs.

THE PATTERN IS STATED AS A PATTERN OVER FOUR OWNED WORDS, NEVER AS A PRODUCTIVE TEST, on the b2_gen_pl_full fleeting-e precedent C1-SPINE cites for exactly this genre (O12 restates the ban on fabricated forms because C1's alternation units are where the temptation is strongest). The four alternations shown are r->rz (dobry->dobrzy), w->wi (nowy->nowi), d->dz (mlody->mlodzi) and n->ni (zmeczony->zmeczeni). The framing that makes it ONE new thing rather than four: THE LEARNER ALREADY DOES THIS TO THE NOUNS. b1_virile_nom taught 'look at the last consonant of the stem' with student-> studenci, Polak->Polacy, lekarz->lekarze. Slide 2 says outright that the adjective in front makes the same move, so this is one familiar operation reaching a second word class, not a new system.

THE SPINE'S OWN TWO NAMED FORMS ARE DROPPED AND THAT IS THE UNIT'S ONE REAL FORK, logged loudly. C1-SPINE names mali, duzi and zmeczeni. zmeczeni is built. mali and duzi are NOT, because NO VIRILE NOUN THIS COURSE OWNS COLLOCATES WITH A SIZE ADJECTIVE. The taught virile nouns are studenci, lekarze, nauczyciele, pracownicy, kelnerzy, Polacy, pacjenci, klienci, artysci, rolnicy, Anglicy, goscie, kibice, przyjaciele, turysci, ludzie, kucharze, dziennikarze, policjanci, informatycy and rodzice - every one an adult occupational or relational noun, and 'mali studenci' / 'duzi lekarze' is not something anyone says. The natural home for mali is chlopcy or synowie, both verified NEW. Rather than ship a table row that never appears in a sentence, the unit substitutes NOWI - which the spine did not name and which is the strongest virile adjective in the pool: nowi studenci, nowi klienci, nowi pracownicy are all completely ordinary Polish, and nowy/nowa/nowe are ALL TAUGHT, so it supplies a perfect four-way distractor set. MLODZI is the second substitution, on the same test. This is the c1_adj_pl_loc precedent applied a second time in the same block: a spine example is a sketch, not a licence. IF JAMES WANTS mali AND duzi, the cost is one new virile noun (chlopcy) and they slot into c1_adj_pl_gym without disturbing anything here.

THE DISTRACTOR SETS DROVE THE ADJECTIVE CHOICE, exactly as they did in c1_adj_pl_gen. Only four adjectives in the whole course have masculine, feminine AND non-virile plural all taught - dobry, nowy, maly, duzy - and of those only dobry and nowy have a usable virile. zmeczony gets its full four-way set because this unit teaches the two missing members itself (zmeczone, zmeczeni), which is why it carries the sharpest items. mlody has mlody/mloda/mlodszy owned but mlode is verified NEW, so its item distracts with the comparative rather than with a form the course does not own. NOTHING FABRICATED, nothing untaught: every distractor string in the file is either taught or taught by this pack.

PAYS b2_copular_future's ABSOLUTE FENCE, which is the reason zmeczone is taught here alongside zmeczeni. That pack's note reads: 'PLURAL predicate adjectives are fenced absolutely - zmeczeni / zmeczone are NEW (b1_virile_gym and b1_conditional_pl each record nearly shipping them by mistake, one batch apart). Every plural sentence in this pack takes a place phrase, never an adjective.' Slide 3 and the Jestesmy zmeczeni / Jestesmy zmeczone pair are that fence paid. The plural predicate itself is NOT new - a2_plural_nom already shipped Koty sa male and Hotele sa dobre - so what slide 3 adds is only that in the plural the choice stops being man/woman and becomes men-group / everything else.

THE ACCUSATIVE IS THE UNIT'S SECOND CONSEQUENCE AND IS DELIBERATELY BUILT ON OWNED STRINGS ONLY. Virile Accusative plural = Genitive plural, on both the noun and the adjective. Every form it needs is already taught: dobrych/nowych ← c1_adj_pl_gen [182], and studentow/kolegow/klientow ← b2_num_virile [157], lekarzy/nauczycieli ← b2_gen_pl_full [155]. HOMOGRAPH DISCIPLINE, named on slide 4 rather than left to sting: every one of those noun forms was taught AS A GENITIVE PLURAL and is used here in the ACCUSATIVE. That is the honest masculine-animate exception AGENTS names (brata/psa/kota are genuinely identical in both cases), one number up, and b2_adj_gen already taught the singular fact. It is stated in one line and anchored on Znam brata. mlodzi, zmeczeni and nowi have NO Accusative here - mlodych, zmeczonych are verified NEW - so the Accusative runs on dobry and nowy only. Logged rather than hidden.

THE NON-VIRILE SIDE IS ENTIRELY RECYCLED and that is what keeps the load at one new thing: te + -e is a2_plural_nom [55], including its own explicit slide-6 fact that the Accusative plural equals the Nominative plural for everything non-virile (Mam nowe ksiazki). dobre/nowe/male/duze are the four non-virile plurals that pack owns; dobre and nowe carry every contrast row here. VERIFIED rather than assumed: check_new.py reports dobre first at a1_gender_check [6] and male at trunk_adjectives_a1 [8], i.e. as NEUTER SINGULARS, so the homograph was checked directly against a2_plural_nom's own items - Czy hotele sa dobre?, Lekcje sa dobre., Koty sa male., Domy sa duze., Mam nowe ksiazki. - which use all four squarely as non-virile plurals. glodne is the counter-example and is FENCED: it is TAUGHT (trunk_adjectives_a1 [8]) but only as a neuter singular, and no later pack ever puts it in a plural, so it appears nowhere in this file.

THE WOMEN-ONLY ROW IS THE UNIT'S SHARPEST DISCRIMINATION and gets two items and a slide row, because the predictable error is 'people take the men-group form'. Corki sa zmeczone and Jestesmy zmeczone say the opposite: the category is masculine-personal, not human. This is the same guard b2_num_virile built its whole feminine defence around (osoba is feminine, so piec osob and never pieciu), one paradigm on.

ci IS USED IN ITS b1_virile_reco JOB ONLY - the virile nominative demonstrative, 'these people'. b1_virile_reco's note flagged in advance that b1_dative_pron [120] would later re-teach the same string as the 2sg dative clitic (podoba ci sie); that second sense appears nowhere in this file, in any stage, and no dative construction is used.

FENCED, all verified NEW and appearing nowhere including as distractors: mali, duzi, starzy, wysocy, wszyscy, mlode, mlodych, zajeci, zajeta, zajete, chorzy, chore, glodni, stare, mile, madrzy, zmeczonych; the virile nouns chlopcy, mezczyzni, panowie, synowie, koledzy; and the Genitive plurals pacjentow, turystow, ludzi, gosci, Polakow, Anglikow - which is why the Accusative items run on studentow, kolegow, klientow, lekarzy and nauczycieli and on no other noun. oni/one are TAUGHT (b1_virile_past [111]) and sit in the auditor's GLUE_LEMMAS where it cannot see them; they are used nowhere, because the Jestesmy pair carries the same contrast without a bare pronoun subject and AGENTS calls pronoun-plus-verb Uzycie items pro-drop-degenerate.

PISANIE: nine items - eight two-word Nominative and Accusative phrases (the c1_adj_pl_gen / c1_adj_pl_dat shape: the Nominative needs no governor, so adjective + noun is the whole minimal pattern unit) and the Jestesmy zmeczeni / Jestesmy zmeczone pair, two words each, verb + predicate adjective with no bolted-on part - the b1_wrapup #0 'Planuje spotkanie.' precedent the repair queue settled, and the same shape c1_existential's whole Pisanie stage used one block earlier. Under the 3-word cap, pattern units not composed sentences; nothing added to the repair queue. All nine answers distinct under the engine's own norm().

TITLE CORRECTED AT THE WIRE, as C1-SPINE's build protocol demands and as batch 1 and batch 2 both had to do. The planned tree label read 'Mali, duzi, zmeczeni' - two of those three forms are no longer taught by this unit (see the fork above), so the label would have carried Polish the course never teaches into learner-visible chrome. Retitled to the house contrast pattern on b1_virile_reco's own 'Ci czy te?' model: DOBRZY CZY DOBRE? - both words owned, and it names the split the unit exists for.

intro.title: The form you have been reading since B1
intro.body: A plural that includes at least one man takes ci rather than te — and it takes a different adjective too. You met dobrzy in B1 as a ready-made form with no rule behind it. Here is the rule, and three more adjectives that follow it. Every other plural keeps the -e form you have had since A2.

rows: studenci — men, or a mixed group

intro.title: The last consonant changes — the same move you already make on the nouns
intro.body: B1 taught you to look at the last consonant of the stem: student becomes studenci, Polak becomes Polacy. The adjective in front does exactly the same thing — the consonant softens and the ending becomes -i, spelled -y after rz. These are the four adjectives this course gives you the form for. It is a pattern to recognise, not a test to run on new words.

headers: A group with a man in it

intro.title: Jesteśmy zmęczeni
intro.body: After być the adjective agrees with the subject, which you have done in the singular since A1 — Jestem zmęczony, Jestem zmęczona — and in the plural since A2, with Koty są małe. What is new is which way the plural splits. It is no longer man against woman. It is a group with a man in it against everything else, and a women-only group counts as everything else.

rows: a group with at least one man

intro.title: As an object, the men-group borrows the Genitive
intro.body: For things and for women-only groups the object form is simply the subject form — that is the A2 rule and it has not changed. For a group with a man in it, both the noun and the adjective borrow the Genitive instead. You have seen this borrowing before in the singular: Znam brata uses the same form as the Genitive too.

match.en: We are tired. (a group with a man in it)

quiz.explain: studenci is a group with men in it, so the adjective takes the men-group form. młody is one man and młodszy is the comparative, younger.
Shops are things, so nothing changes — the -e plural you have had since A2. nowi is only for a group with a man in it.
lekarze is a men-group plural. dobre would be right for films, shops or a women-only group.

quiz.prompt: We are tired. — said by three women →
quiz.explain: No man in the group, so it takes the everything-else form. zmęczona is one woman on her own.

quiz.prompt: We are tired. — said by two men and a woman →
quiz.explain: One man in the group is enough. Polish does not wait for a majority.
The stem's last consonant softens: zmęczony, zmęczeni. Same move as dobry to dobrzy, on a different consonant.
This is the one worth slowing down for. Daughters are people, but they are not men, and the special form is about men rather than about people. A women-only group takes the same form as things do.
As an object, a men-group plural borrows the Genitive — on the noun and on the adjective alike. dobrzy studenci is the subject form.
kolegów already does duty for both the Genitive and the Accusative, and the adjective copies it. The last two are the Dative and the Instrumental from earlier in this block.
Films are things, so the object form is exactly the subject form — the A2 rule, untouched. The other three all borrow something they should not: only a group with a man in it does that.
nowy ends in w, and w softens to wi before the ending. The written form looks small; it is the same change dobry makes to dobrzy.
te and dobre go together, and kobiety takes te. ci and dobrzy both need at least one man in the group.

type_items.prompt_en: the good students (subject form, a group with men in it)
the new clients (subject form, a group with men in it)
type_items.explain: w softens to wi: nowy, nowi.

type_items.prompt_en: the young doctors (subject form, a group with men in it)
type_items.explain: d softens to dz: młody, młodzi.

type_items.prompt_en: the tired teachers (subject form, a group with men in it)

type_items.explain: A women-only group takes the everything-else form, not the men-group one.

type_items.prompt_en: the good students (object form, a group with men in it)
type_items.explain: The object form of a men-group plural is the Genitive, borrowed whole.

type_items.prompt_en: We are tired. (a group with a man in it)

use_items.explain: Córki is a women-only plural, so it takes zmęczone — the same form things take. The men-group form is about men, not about people.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: I know the good students.

use_items.explain: Nothing borrows anything here — films are things, so the object form is the plain plural you have had since A2.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: The films are good, but the shops are new.
use_items.answer: Filmy są dobre, ale sklepy są nowe.
accepts: Filmy są dobre, ale sklepy są nowe.

use_items.answer: Nauczyciele są zmęczeni, ale studenci są młodzi.
